text:
jonah: Quick sync — planning a controlled head-to-head run for two model variants to isolate runtime differences (kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache behavior). need volunteers to lock down the methodology.

maria: count me in. want to avoid any nondeterminism in tokenizer and decode params.

ash: +1. checklist: same prompt corpus, same tokenizer version, identical decode params (temp, top_p, seed), explicit stop sequences, and consistent cache warm/cold definitions.

lena: for KV cache tests we should do: cold (first request after restart), warm (same session, cached prefixes), and primed (explicit prefix put into cache). also capture per-step KV hit ratios.

kevin: agreed. also: hold batch shaping constant across runs — i.e. per-stream max_tokens and per-batch target_tokens. that kills a lot of noisy perf variance.

jonah: proposal for run config — paste below, please comment if anything missing: 
```
run_config:
  model: mix-13b-v1
  tokenizer_version: 2025-11-08
  decode:
    temperature: 0.0
    top_p: 0.95
    seed: 42
    max_new_tokens: 128
    stop_sequences: ["\n\n"]
  traffic:
    mode: replay
    seed_sessions: "prod-replay-2025-11"
  runtime:
    batch_target_tokens: 2048
    batch_max_latency_ms: 50
    concurrency_per_stream: 1
    kv_cache_policy: manual_priming
  kernel_hints: ["fused_attn","matmul_wmma","int8_kernels"]
```

maria: please ensure tokenizer normalization flags exactly match production (case folding, control char stripping). small tokenizer mismatches change token counts -> decode length -> kernel paths.

ash: for apples-to-apples decoding we must also make generation deterministic: disable sampling, set `temperature=0` and `top_p=1.0` if using nucleus sampling fallback. otherwise diffs are noisy.

lena: instrumentation checklist: per-request latency trace, per-token GPU utilization, NVTX ranges, kernel selection log (which kernel chosen per op), KV cache hits, and CPU-side queue times. add a tiny tracer to record sequence length distribution seen by kernels.

kevin: how do we handle continuous batching effects vs simulated fixed batches? my suggestion: run both modes — (A) live continuous batching with the runtime's default batching logic, (B) forced-fixed batching where we pad to target_tokens and disable batch coalescing. compare.

jonah: good. and include synthetic microbenchmarks (toy prompt set) + replay harness (exact prod prompts). label runs clearly: "synthetic_live", "synthetic_fixed", "replay_live", "replay_fixed", and KV variants: "cold", "warm", "primed".

maria: recording note: always capture tokenizer token counts per prompt. mismatches explain p95 differences.

perfbot: run scheduled: 2025-11-28T09:00:00Z by @jonah. quick summary report will be posted to this thread when complete.

jonah: after runs finish we should do an apples-to-apples comparison of: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU SM util, memory pressure, kernel call counts, and end-to-end correctness diffs (exact string compare + normalized-WS compare).

ash: also compute per-kernel cumulative time and percent-of-total. often one bad matmul kernel dominates.

lena: regression handling: if new kernel selection causes >10% p95 regression in any traffic label, roll back kernel hints and re-run. capture delta stack traces for the top 3 slow requests.

kevin: small benchmark tip — cap the number of concurrent sessions so we aren't saturating host-level NIC or PCIe. keep GPU utilization in 60-85% target so we can see per-request micro variance.

jonah: agreed. final deliverables: (1) run artifacts (traces + kernel logs + raw output), (2) summary CSV with all metrics, (3) a small Jupyter notebook that reproduces the p95 table and plots kernel-level flame-percentages.

maria: i can own the notebook. ash will collect traces. lena will add KV instrumentation. kevin will manage traffic harness settings.

jonah: thanks — will kick off. ping here when you upload artifacts. :rocket:
